title: Lineage II vegetation-architect ecology
scope: Primary feeding strategy and landscape effects of Project Hearthway's developing Lineage II crown and ribbon branches; usable within shared-setting fauna and regional-ecology development.
claims: Crown forms use short, reinforced mouth-rays to split and process tough mature stalks, brush, and woody growth.
Crown feeding and movement help maintain open corridors and vegetation mosaics.
Ribbon forms use longer tactile mouth-rays to selectively harvest shoots, fruiting bodies, and lakeshore or woodland-edge vegetation.
Ribbon feeding shapes woodland-edge and wet-margin vegetation at a finer scale than crown herds.
Seasonal movements by the two branches can materially affect roads, fields, woodland edges, soil fertility, and settlement defences where their ranges overlap human land.
boundaries: This record does not establish final lineage or species names, complete taxonomy, or every member's diet.

Digestive architecture is governed separately by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/lineage-ii-fermentation-lattice, two-stage symbiont inheritance by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/lineage-ii-symbiont-inheritance, and the broad migration and initial-settlement relationship by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/lineage-ii-peripheral-migration-corridor; exact oral anatomy, chamber anatomy, transfer mechanisms, route geometry, seasonal timing and direction, herd scale, breeding seasons, and winter strategies remain undefined.

A major open-ground forage guild is governed separately by canon://world/shared-universe-001/ecology/basin-reserve-web-vegetation-guild; exact guild species, anatomy, chemistry, distribution, productivity, and the complete seasonal diets of either branch remain undefined.
Species-level omnivory or specialist symbioses remain possible when independently supported.
No domestication, hunting practice, material use, taboo, law, or cultural interpretation is established.
No System level, reward source, trait payload, specialised Mana organ, or Ancestry Development mechanic is established.
story_implications: Settlements within crown migration range need seasonal field, road, and defensive practices responsive to herd movement.
Ribbon populations can create recurring lower-intensity conflict around gardens, managed woodland, and lake-margin resources.
The same animals may be regarded as destructive, useful, valuable, or culturally important by different livelihoods and communities.
system_implications: This record is a world-level ecological input compatible with CAL0 creature and ecology rules.
Any Mana reinforcement or progression later assigned to these animals requires separate causal and CAL0 review.
research_questions: Which additional original vegetation lineages complement the reserve-web guild across the seasonal diets of each branch?
How does the fermentation lattice integrate anatomically with oral processing and the internal brood chamber?
How quickly can the slow-breeding populations expand or recolonise newly available habitat?
Which exact corridor branches, seasonal timings, and herd scales implement the approved peripheral migration pattern around the initial settlement's catchment?
